title: Preweek communications — tightrope brief for short-notice patch
content:
Context:
- We need to push a short, low-risk kernel-side patch to a small subset of dedicated hosts next Tue-Wed window. Patch was approved but rollout timeline slipped — stakeholders want a limited announcement to customers and internal ops comms ready in case of noise.
- This doc = my scratch for what to say, rapid Q&A, and manager talking points. Will shape into a tidy slack/email once we confirm times.
Audience:
- Primary: oncall SREs, solutions engineering (customer-facing escalation), product ops (billing/alerts), and Eng managers running Dedicated accounts.
- Secondary: CS reps for affected customers (heads-up only), legal/compliance if any contracts need note.
TL;DR (single line to paste):
- Rolling a small safety patch to a subset of Dedicated hosts Tue 03/17 02:00–05:00 PT; expected impact: brief degraded request throughput for 5–15m per host during kernel swap. No customer action expected.
Key constraints / what we absolutely want to avoid saying:
- Do not use absolutes like "no impact" — we expect a short throughput dip on some hosts.
- Avoid technical jargon in external-facing lines ("kernel swap", "rebootstrap"); keep external phrasing to "brief degraded request throughput" or "short latency blips".
- Don’t promise rollback timelines beyond our runbook — if rollback is needed, say "we will prioritize rollback and updates every 15 minutes".
Core messages (internal):
- Why: safety/security hardening that reduces rare crash surface; required by infra roadmap and validated in canary.
- Scope: 18 Dedicated nodes (region: us-west-2), canary completed on 3 nodes.
- Risk: low but non-zero. Expected symptoms: transient latency spikes and increased 5xxs for up to 15 minutes on a node during its patch cycle.
- Rollout plan: staggered, automation-managed (ansible/auto-run), human-checkpoint after first 3 nodes.
External short message templates (CS/customer-facing):
- Email/Support blurb subject: "Planned maintenance — short patch on select Dedicated hosts (Mar 17)"
- Body (2 sentences): "We’ll be performing a short maintenance patch to a small set of dedicated hosts on Mar 17 between 02:00–05:00 PT. You should not need to take any action; you may see brief increases in latency or retries for a few minutes on affected hosts. If you see persistent errors, please open a support ticket quoting INFRA-4821."
Slack alert (internal #ops):
- "Heads-up: rolling safety patch to 18 Dedicated nodes in us-west-2 Tue 03/17 02:00–05:00 PT. Expect brief latency blips (5–15m) per node during its patch window. Canary ok. Oncall: @riley (primary) / @aisha (backup)."
Manager talking points (for quick syncs / 1:1s):
- "Canary passed; patches are low-risk. We have human gate after first 3 nodes. If any significant regression, we will pause and rollback. CS has the short blurb. Priority = keep customer-facing messaging calm and factual."
Proactive Q&A (drafts to prep answers quickly):
- Q: "Will my Dedicated cluster be taken offline?"
  A: "No — clusters remain available. Individual hosts may serve degraded throughput briefly while being patched; autoscaling/failover will handle most traffic. We’ll monitor and act if we see sustained issues."
- Q: "How long will this take per host?"
  A: "Host-level window ~5–15 minutes (patch + validation). Our staggered schedule means your cluster should not be wholly disrupted."
- Q: "Can you guarantee zero data loss?"
  A: "We have no reason to expect data loss. The patch is designed as an in-place update; standard replication/ack guarantees remain in place."
- Q: "What happens if rollback is required?"
  A: "We will pause the rollout, perform rollback on affected nodes, and issue an update every 15 minutes until stable."
- Q: "Who to call if a customer escalates?"
  A: "Oncall SRE first, then Solutions Eng if it escalates to account impact. See escalation list below."
Escalation / contact list (quick):
- oncall SRE: Riley Chen (@riley)
- backup: Aisha Malik (@aisha)
- Solutions Eng lead: Rowan Patel
- Product ops: J. Nguyen (billing)
- CS escalation cell: ops-escalations@redwood.example.com
Rapid playbook checklist (tickets & action items):
- [ ] Confirm final patch binary & checksum (owner: Rowan) — needed by Fri EOD 03/13
- [ ] Lock down runbook steps and rollback commands in Confluence (owner: Riley) — Sat 03/14
- [ ] Send internal pre-announce to #ops and #dedicated-provisioning (owner: Aisha) — Mon 03/16
- [ ] Draft CS support blurb & set canned responses (owner: CS lead) — Mon 03/16
- [ ] Ensure monitoring dashboards have alert thresholds (owner: SRE metrics) — Mon 03/16
- [ ] Final go/no-go call 60m before start (owner: patch lead)
Notes to self / open questions (feel free to edit):
- Confirm timezones with APAC customers? We are doing small subset in us-west-2; likely minimal APAC exposure but call it out if any customers have strict SLAs.
- Does Legal want a heads-up? Probably not for low-risk patch but check with compliance for tier-1 enterprise names.
- Should we pre-warn select top-10 dedicated customers? Solutions Eng input needed — lean conservative (no pre-warn) unless account has historically sensitive SLAs.
- Consider a short post-mortem template prepared in advance (2 bullet points: what, impact, follow-ups).
Draft Slack cadence (internal updates during window):
- T-minus 60: "Starting in 60m: patch window for 18 Dedicated nodes in us-west-2. Canary passed. Oncall: @riley"
- T-plus 0: "Patch started on node X. Expect ~10m of higher latency on this node."
- T-plus 10m: "Node X patched and validated. No action required. Moving to node Y."
- On any issue: "PAUSE — node X showing >1% 5xxs over 5m. Investigating; will decide rollback in next 10m."
Formatting plan for final external email/support article (short):
- Subject line, 2-sentence explanation, expected customer impact (plain language), link to status page, support contact and incident key. Keep minimal.
Final: this is grooming text — rough, blunt. Convert to tidy slack+support doc after runbook and owners locked. Save a copy to confluence under infra/short-patch-playbook-2026 when final.
